scope: Proposition 5.4 (Finite-level spectral facts) of the manuscript “Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level” (preprints/Ramanujan-Arthur-Decompositions-of-Cuspidal-Functions-at-Full-Finite-Level-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b4b0cfe23007d159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At a fixed compact open level the following assertions hold. (i) The discrete summand DK of LK is finite-dimensional. Its orthogonal complement admits a Hecke-equivariant unitary realization as a closed invariant subspace of a finite sum of direct integrals of normalized parabolic inductions Ind G(AF ) P(AF )(σ ⊗ χ), where P is proper, σ belongs to the discrete spectrum of its Levi M, and χ ranges over a compact torus of unitary unramified characters, subject to the central condition imposed by Ξ. All fixed-level fiber dimensions are bounded. (ii) Let Qb be the orthogonal projection onto the point basis in an HN ball of radius b. There are constants C, c > 0 such that ∥(1 − Qb)v∥ ≤ Ce−cb ∥v∥ (v ∈ DK, b ≥ 0). (5.14) (iii) Suppose that the level at x is Iwahori. The ordered Bernstein weights of a fiber induced from M have the form w(tM z), wΦ+ M ⊂ Φ+ G, (5.15) where tM is an ordered Bernstein weight of σx and z is the local value of χ. There are finitely many such weight families, and their generalized-weight lengths are uniformly bounded.
